sections.value:
PASS WITH NOTES: S240-001 closed; no blocking security or normal-use correctness finding.

Head: 520e5d196305eb61a668bba93257719f0095272f
Round-2 request: 01a1ecb9-e9e8-76d2-9c6f-e938ccbaeb59
Reviewed delta: 69c0516d8879793b1776753e6d75839931608ce0..520e5d196305eb61a668bba93257719f0095272f and necessary context. Final round under C34; no expanded audit or additional gate. No local builds/tests, dependency installation or product-source edits.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| - | - | - | - | No unresolved vulnerability found in the reviewed delta | - |

S240-001 closure:
The first recognized harness host now terminates the ancestry walk. That host's PID and recorded start must both match the seat; a registered outer Copilot A cannot supply the identity of an inner, unregistered Copilot B. Shell wrappers remain traversable. Both pane and paneless identity paths use the guard (crates/cli/src/statusline.rs:326-408). The nested-host regression pins direct and wrapped A/B cases and correct own-seat display, including PID recycling (crates/cli/src/statusline_tests.rs:666-846).

Normal invocation and false-negative check:
The managed shell script execs pij-rs, without adding a node helper (harness/scripts/copilot-statusline-pij.sh:12). Native registration selects the nearest Copilot ancestor and submits that host's PID/start, not the extension child or outer node launcher (.copilot/extensions/pij/store.mjs:435-436,2512-2544). This agrees with the retained live observation: this review seat records native copilot PID 49835; its node launcher PID 49833 is ABOVE it. A bounded 20-second child-only observation saw eight pij-rs processes directly below copilot. It read no argv, so it does not prove each child's purpose or every possible future helper topology. This CLI build's documentation does not specify helper ancestry. No actual normal-use false negative was established; a hypothetical intermediate harness-named helper is not a new round-two gate.

Platform and suffix fix:
macOS reuses the checked ProcBSDShortInfo reader for parent and name. The 16-byte name field includes its NUL terminator; all recognized host names fit. Linux strips exactly one trailing " (deleted)" from the executable filename, matching existing registration normalization and avoiding a false negative after an in-place executable upgrade (crates/harnesses/src/proc.rs:339-399; crates/daemon/src/registration.rs:2043-2052). The suffix regression is at proc.rs:717-726. These reads use in-process APIs, not shell commands, PATH lookup, ps or tmux.

Cost delta:
Zero new child launches and zero additional daemon requests per render. The existing whoami request and existing statusline invocation remain. Linux adds an executable-link read for each inspected process; macOS gets parent/name in the same existing syscall. Direct ancestry needs two parent/name observations and one start observation. The walk's precise ceiling is self plus 64 ancestors, at most 65 parent/name observations, not 64 total (crates/cli/src/statusline.rs:390-408; crates/cli/src/main.rs:2573-2613). Scale is O(min(depth,64)) per render per Copilot session: configured 10-second periodic refresh plus event-driven renders, with no changed cadence, loop or timer. This is a zero-NEW-launch claim, not a claim that the entire existing statusline never launches a process.

C34 follow-up, nonblocking: align the PR's "<=64 reads" cost prose with the self-plus-64-ancestors implementation. This small prose-bound mismatch is not a cost breach. The spawn-site sensor excludes CLI launches, so passing it does not replace direct source inspection or a deployed cost measurement (crates/testkit/tests/spawn_sites.rs:1-12).

F195 proof additions:
The delta now asserts removal of receiver lapse fields from state and list after recovery, and a visible never-renewed diagnosis after boot grace (crates/daemon/src/http/native_tests.rs:2633-2663,2881-2889). These directly improve the previously recorded proof gaps. The cost description now names bulk GET /v1/cards and list's in-memory per-row scan; no delivery/renew loop change is introduced by this delta.

Final-head proof:
- just pr-freeze 240: FINAL at the full head above, clean detached worktree, all five latest checks passed. A superseded cancelled Delivers run is not the latest verdict.
- CI run 44231858379, rust-test job 134558560135: cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --profile ci passed 2474 tests; six excluded tests reported skipped; 138.245 seconds.
- Successful-job JUnit artifact 14395228809, UUID 6b538e86-75cf-404d-a083-0e08d35cbca4, positively confirms the nested-host regression, foreign-seat guard, real host reader, statusline E2E, Linux deleted-suffix regression, native lapse/recovery and never-renewed cases, and spawn-site gates passed. Rust-lint and both Node checks passed; latest Delivers run 44231869562 passed.
- No local harness boot/checks or cargo build/test was run, per the explicit CI-only review rule. Linux CI does not compile macOS; those paths were reviewed by eye, not executed here.

Owed after merge/install/bounce:
Repeat the before/after fleet-cost receipts with paired timestamped same-PID spawn counters, just spawn-rate --seconds 20, and daemon CPU/RSS. Verify registered own-seat, second-server/unregistered and nested-host status lines, plus native receiver lapse/recovery. The first-round baseline remains: 2026-11-18 03:15:28Z-03:15:48Z, daemon PID 46800, total 793 -> 793 with all by_op counters unchanged; machine-wide 108.3 launches/s. No after-deploy measurement is claimed.

Harness improvement: the original review's nested-host counterexample and the replaced-binary edge now have named permanent regression tests, as do the receiver recovery/never-renewed display cases. Remaining macOS execution and future topology coverage are nonblocking proof qualifications, not a third review round.
